title: What does ISO 14001 require for environmental competence and awareness, and what changed in 2026?
description: ISO 14001 clauses 7.2 and 7.3 on environmental competence and awareness, the April 2026 edition and the transition to April 2029, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: ISO 14001, the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) environmental management system standard, requires organizations in clause 7.2 to determine the competence needed by people whose work affects environmental performance and compliance obligations, determine training needs linked to environmental aspects, close gaps and retain evidence. Clause 7.3 requires awareness of the environmental policy, significant aspects, their own contribution and the consequences of nonconformity. ISO 14001:2026 replaced the 2015 edition on April 15, 2026.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2 ties competence to two outcomes: environmental performance and the ability to fulfill compliance obligations.
Clause 7.2 also requires training needs to be determined from the organization's environmental aspects and its environmental management system, a link that ISO 9001 does not make.
Clause 7.3 lists four awareness items, including the significant environmental aspects and impacts associated with each person's work.
ISO lists ISO 14001:2015 as withdrawn on April 15, 2026 and replaced by ISO 14001:2026.
Certification bodies report a 36-month transition: ISO 14001:2015 certificates lose validity on April 30, 2029.
regulator: No regulator: ISO/TC 207/SC 1 maintains the standard; conformity is assessed by accredited certification bodies
appliesTo: Manufacturers and other organizations of any size that operate or seek certification of an environmental management system
Persons doing work under the organization's control whose work affects environmental performance or compliance obligations, including contractors where relevant
Roles connected with significant environmental aspects, such as waste handling, chemical storage, wastewater treatment, emissions control and maintenance

sections.heading: Which edition of ISO 14001 applies as at November 2026?

blocks.text: Both editions are in use during a transition. ISO's [ISO 14001:2015 page](https://www.iso.org/standard/60857.html) lists the third edition, published in September 2015, as withdrawn on April 15, 2026 and revised by ISO 14001:2026. ISO tells organizations certified to the 2015 edition to consult their certification body about transition arrangements.

Certification body [DQS reports](https://www.dqsglobal.com/en/explore/blog/iso-14001-2026-transition) that publication on April 15, 2026 started a 36-month transition and that certificates to ISO 14001:2015 will lose validity on April 30, 2029. The clause descriptions below follow the 2015 text, against which most certificates are still held. Clause 7.2 is competence and clause 7.3 is awareness in both editions, because the 2026 edition follows ISO's harmonized structure for management system standards.

sections.heading: What does clause 7.2 require for competence?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2 requires the organization to define, achieve and evidence competence for people whose work affects environmental outcomes. As summarized by [Auditor Training Online](https://blog.auditortrainingonline.com/blog/iso-14001-clause-7.2), the organization shall:

items: Determine the necessary competence of persons doing work under its control that affects its environmental performance and its ability to fulfill its compliance obligations.
Ensure these persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience.
Determine training needs associated with its environmental aspects and its environmental management system.
Where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken.

blocks.text: The organization must retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence. A note to the clause gives examples of applicable actions: training, mentoring or reassigning current employees, or hiring or contracting competent persons.

Item 3 is what makes ISO 14001 different from ISO 9001. Training needs are derived from the aspects register, so a manufacturer whose significant aspects include solvent emissions, hazardous waste and stormwater discharge should be able to show a line from each aspect to the roles that control it and the competence each role needs. Compliance obligations identified under clause 6.1.3, such as permit conditions, feed into the same analysis.

sections.heading: What does clause 7.3 require for awareness?

blocks.text: Clause 7.3 requires persons doing work under the organization's control to be aware of four things. Based on the [Auditor Training Online summary of clause 7.3](https://blog.auditortrainingonline.com/blog/iso-14001-clause-7.3), these are:

items: **The significant environmental aspects** and related actual or potential environmental impacts associated with their work.
**Their contribution to the effectiveness of the environmental management system**, including the benefits of enhanced environmental performance.
**The implications of not conforming** with the environmental management system requirements, including not fulfilling the organization's compliance obligations.

blocks.text: "Persons doing work under the organization's control" can include employees, contractors, subcontractors, labor hire workers, visitors and volunteers, depending on the work. Clause 7.3 does not itself require documented information, but without records of what was communicated, to whom and when, an organization has little to show an auditor beyond interviews.

sections.heading: What changed in ISO 14001:2026 that affects training?

blocks.text: The 2026 edition is a consolidated revision with limited new requirements. [TÜV Rheinland](https://www.tuv.com/world/en/revision-iso-14001-2026.html) reports that the final draft was published in January 2026 and the standard on April 15, 2026, and that ISO decided after a 2021 user survey not to revise the standard completely.

The main changes TÜV Rheinland lists are a move to the harmonized structure, editorial and terminology changes, greater consideration of environmental conditions including climate change, pollution, resource availability and ecosystem condition, reinforcement of the life cycle perspective, a new clause 6.3 on planning of changes, clearer requirements for documented processes in clauses 8.1 and 8.2, and audit program objectives in clause 9.2.2. Clauses 7.2 and 7.3 are not named among the main changes. The 2024 amendment that added explicit consideration of climate change to the analysis of context was, according to TÜV Rheinland, applied without a transition period.

The training impact is indirect but real. New or reinforced topics such as climate risk, biodiversity, life cycle thinking and change planning will produce new significant aspects and compliance obligations, and clause 7.2 then requires the related training needs to be determined. Organizations should confirm clause wording against the purchased 2026 text before rewriting procedures.

sections.heading: How should a manufacturing site apply these clauses?

blocks.text: Start with the aspects register and work outward. For each significant aspect, name the operational controls, the roles that run them and the competence those roles need, then decide how awareness reaches everyone else in the area.

items: Link chemical handling roles to both the environmental controls and the worker safety duties in [OSHA hazard communication training](/regulations/osha-hazard-communication-training-requirements), so one change event updates both.
Include contractors who manage waste, maintain abatement equipment or work near drains, since they do work under the organization's control.
Integrate the environmental and safety management systems where possible; the parallel clauses are described in [ISO 45001 competence and awareness](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness).
Plan the move to the 2026 edition before April 30, 2029, including any competence updates for internal auditors and environmental staff.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links significant environmental aspects and compliance obligations to concepts and assessment points for the roles that control them. When an aspect, permit or edition of the standard changes, the framework identifies the competence requirements and people affected, which supports both clause 7.2 evidence and transition planning.

faqs.q: Does ISO 14001 require environmental awareness training for all employees?
faqs.a: Clause 7.3 requires all persons doing work under the organization's control to be aware of the environmental policy, relevant significant aspects, their contribution and the implications of nonconformity. It does not mandate a training course or records, but most organizations use induction and toolbox talks and keep records to show auditors.

ISO lists ISO 14001:2015 as withdrawn on April 15, 2026 and replaced by ISO 14001:2026. Certificates to the 2015 edition remain valid during the transition; certification bodies report they lose validity on April 30, 2029.

faqs.q: How does ISO 14001 competence differ from ISO 9001 competence?
faqs.a: The structure is the same, but ISO 14001 ties competence to environmental performance and compliance obligations, and requires training needs to be determined from environmental aspects and the environmental management system. ISO 9001 ties competence to quality management system performance and product or service conformity.

faqs.q: Do contractors fall under ISO 14001 competence and awareness requirements?
faqs.a: Yes, where they do work under the organization's control that affects environmental performance or compliance obligations. Clause 7.2 and 7.3 apply to persons doing work under the organization's control, which can include contractors, subcontractors and labor hire workers.
